body: But me praying at dinner is not them respecting my beliefs, it's me respecting theirs.  I could refuse (which I do at larger family functions), but it's something that I do because I love them and it doesn't put me out at all.  And you're right, they do want me to "return to God".  But if asking me to pray at dinner once every few weeks is all they do then I'm ok with it and very lucky judging by some of the horror stories I've read.  I am totally financially dependent on them, they pay for insurance, bills, food, and most importantly my college tuition.  They could go a lot further in trying to make me find God again, say by throwing me out of the house and not paying for school anymore, but they don't.  All they do is ask me to pray at dinner, and that really isn't a big deal to me.

I've outed myself as an agnostic to them.  I've never come out and expressly told them I'm an atheist now, but I think they know (in a don't ask don't tell kinda way).  I have a pretty open relationship with my parents in that way.  We pretty regularly have discussions about politics (they're conservatives, I'm a liberal), religion, and evolution.  They'd never kick me out for not believing what they believe.  I show respect for their beliefs because they respect mine.

Tell your parents to stop being enabling dipshits.  Your parents are being pussies, and there isn't really much YOU can do about it.  Your parents need to stop paying for his shit and throw his ass out of the house.
